study.title: The low-frequency BOLD signal oscillation response in the insular associated to immediate analgesia of ankle acupuncture in patients with chronic low back pain
study.population: Right-handed patients diagnosed with chronic low back pain (CLBP), originally recruited from Hangzhou Red Cross Hospital
study.inclusion_criteria: 1) aged between 18 and 65 years; 2) had a disease duration of ≥6 months; 3) were experiencing pain intensity of at least 3 (VAS=0–10)
study.exclusion_criteria: 1) accompanied with pain unrelated to the present diagnosis, or suffering from psychiatric, or neurological disorders, or serious infections; 2) had MRI contraindications, such as claustrophobia; 3) showed contraindications for acupuncture, such as bleeding tendency and pregnancy; 4) had received any therapies within the past 5 days; 5) consumed alcohol within 10 hours preceding the first scan; 6) had head motion that exceeded 2 mm in translation or 2° in rotation during scans; 7) reported a different level of local sensation between the two interventions

arms.arm_label_exact: patients with chronic low back pain receiving ankle acupuncture
arms.dropouts: Two participants excluded due to significant head motion (>2 mm/2°)

conditions.timepoint_exact: 8-minute resting-state scan immediately after tactile stimulation
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI scan following tactile stimulation (needle pricking skin without penetration); participants kept eyes closed and not thinking of anything in particular

conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI scan during retention of ankle acupuncture needle; participants kept eyes closed and not thinking of anything in particular

acupoints_used_exact: ankle zone 5 of the left leg
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: ankle zone 5 of the left leg, located at the crosspoint of three-finger width above the lateral malleolus and posterior margin
interventions.needle_type_exact: disposable silver acupuncture needles (0.35×40 mm; Taihe Brand, Beijing, China)

interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: AA is a type of subcutaneous acupuncture developed in the 1970s; it requires only the insertion of a single needle with no further manual manipulation; AA exerts therapeutic effects similar to those induced by traditional acupuncture in the treatment of pain

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Functional images: gradient-echo EPI (implied); 3D T1-weighted structural images
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: functional: 43 contiguous axial slices, slice thickness 1.33 mm, matrix size 64×64, FOV 200×200 mm2; structural: 128 slices, slice thickness 1 mm, matrix size 256×256, FOV 256×256 mm2; resampled to 3×3×3 mm3
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 8'00'' per functional scan; 5'05'' structural scan; time interval between rest1 and rest2 was 15 minutes
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: 6 mm full width-half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: head motion exceeding 2 mm in translation or 2° in rotation; first 10 time points discarded
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: 0.01–0.08 Hz (low-frequency band); fALFF also uses 0–0.25 Hz (entire frequency range with TR=2 seconds)
statistical_thresholds_exact: voxel-wise P<0.05, cluster-wise P<0.05, two-tailed test; minimum cluster size of 10; connection criteria (rmm)=5 (edge connected); Gaussian random field theory (GRF)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Gaussian random field theory (GRF) correction (voxel-wise P<0.05, cluster-wise P<0.05)

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 labels the ALFF result in the insular as 'rest1' in the results text but the contrast is rest2 vs rest1 (ankle acupuncture vs tactile stimulation). The text states 'ALFF values of four clusters significantly altered during the scan after the insertion of the needle (ie, rest1)' which appears to be a typographic error — the paper clearly states rest2 is after needle insertion and rest1 is after tactile stimulation. This is confirmed by context throughout the methods and results.

In the ALFF result section, the paper states 'the scan after tactile stimulation (ie, rest2)' which appears to be a typographical swap — rest1 is after tactile stimulation and rest2 is after AA insertion. Extraction has followed the correct definitions as given in the methods and study paradigm.
The paper does not report expectancy, credibility, or allocation guessing measures beyond the local sensation NRS equivalence.
Adverse events are not explicitly mentioned or reported in the paper.
The paper does not specify the flip angle for functional images explicitly in the text (FA of 90° is stated). Structural FA is stated as 8°.
The PMID is not provided in the document; only the DOI (10.2147/JPR.S189390) is available.

The correlation between ALFF in the left insular spherical ROI (MNI -57, 12, 6; radius 6 mm) and VAS scores (Figure 5A) uses a slightly different coordinate from Table 1 ALFF cluster peak (-57, 12, 6 vs cluster MNI -57, 12, 6 — these are the same). However, fALFF cluster peak is -57, 9, -3. The overlapping cluster for the ALFF change vs VAS change correlation is described as 'overlapping area of statistically significant ALFF and fALFF maps' located in the left insular, shown in Figure 5B, but exact coordinates of the overlap are not tabulated.
Table 1 lists two separate PG (precentral gyrus) clusters both in the right hemisphere (R). They have been extracted as two separate rows (PG1 and PG2) as tabulated.

The paper does not report individual subject demographics (sex breakdown given as five females, seven males; mean age 44.42±6.99 years; pain duration 7.58±6.60 years) at the arm level since there is only one arm.
The study is not randomized; it is a within-subject design with a fixed order (tactile stimulation always precedes ankle acupuncture). No randomization of condition order is reported.

The label 'right cuneus' appears in the results text ('increased in the right cuneus (T-value=3.57)') but Table 1 labels the same cluster as 'Precuneus/OL/PL' with hemisphere 'L' and coordinates 15, -90, 36. The x-coordinate of 15 is positive (right hemisphere) but the table labels it 'L'. This is a potential inconsistency in the paper. The coordinate has been extracted as reported in Table 1.

Supplementary Figures S1 and S2 show individual and group ALFF and fALFF values within significant clusters, but no numerical data from these figures are extractable beyond what is described in the text.
The paper does not report global signal regression explicitly; only WM and CSF signal regression and Friston-24 head motion parameters are mentioned as nuisance regressors.
Peak-only re-extraction: 0 contrasts updated, 2 new contrasts added
